abstract:
Abstract
                  Signaling theory predicts that communication, such as by CEOs, might complement observable environmental engagement by a firm, by reducing information asymmetry. Yet it remains unclear whether firms with stronger environmental engagement communicate more about these efforts and the potential implications for firm value. To analyze 14,523 firm-quarter earnings call Q&A sessions held by 364 publicly listed firms between 2007 and 2022, the current research measures CEO communication about firm environmental engagement and the communicative intent behind such communication by combining MSCI Environmental Pillar Scores, Compustat data, and a fine-tuned DeBERTa model. Firms with stronger environmental engagement communicate less, rather than more, about their efforts during earnings call Q&A sessions. Yet CEO communication about firm environmental engagement can be positively associated with firm value, depending on the communicative intent the CEO indicates, such that assertive and directive speech maintain this positive association, but expressive and commissive speech acts are negatively associated with firm value.

ob.tldr: 基于14,523次财报电话会问答，结合MSCI环境评分、Compustat数据与微调DeBERTa，检验CEO环境沟通意图及企业价值关系。环境参与更强的企业反而沟通更少；断言式、指令式沟通与价值正相关，表达式、承诺式则负相关。

title: CEO environmental communication, speech acts, and firm value
title_zh: CEO环境沟通、言语行为与企业价值
